Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- Internet sensation Susan Boyle came up short, coming in second during "Britain's Got Talent" finale on Saturday. Fans cheering on Susan Boyle react after she comes in second during "Britain's Got Talent." Boyle was upset by winner Diversity, a 10-person dance group from Essex and East London, England, ranging in age from 12 to 25 years old. The group won 100,000 British pounds ($161,000) and will perform for Queen Elizabeth II in the Royal Variety Show. "The best people won," Boyle said. The dancers appeared shocked Saturday when it was announced that they had won. The group was formed in 2007, and in the same year won the United Kingdom Dance Championships. The group's choreographer "tries to create a dance style that is eye-catching and entertaining" and uses films such as 2007's "Transformers" for inspiration, the show's site said. Boyle wowed the crowd Saturday night with an encore performance of the song that first made her so famous around the world -- "I Dreamed a Dream," from the musical "Les Miserables." After her performance Saturday, the crowd and judges gave Boyle, who wore a floor-length gown, a standing ovation.  Boyle finishes second » . "You had the nerve to come back here tonight, face your critics and beat them," judge Simon Cowell told her. "You did it." Boyle had vowed to leave the television show before the finale, after a hectic week, but recanted and performed at the finale Saturday. The 48-year-old Scottish singer wowed audiences and judges during her audition in April when she belted out "I Dreamed a Dream." Her performance earned her a string of global television appearances. During the semifinals Sunday, she started off by missing the first note of her performance of "Memory" from the musical, "Cats."  Watch Boyle's semifinal performance » . She redeemed herself to earn a standing ovation and a spot in Saturday's finale. The global fame and the "odd bit of negative press" in the past week have been too overwhelming for her, judge Piers Morgan told CNN's "Larry King Live" on Friday. "She's just had a pretty rough week because I think the full enormity of what has happened to her is beginning to hit home," Morgan said. "Earlier this week, she had a lot of tears. ... At one stage, she was going to leave the show. So, fortunately, we've calmed everything down."  Watch how Boyle may be feeling the pressure » . Boyle said that that she has put the tumultuous week behind her and is getting ready for the finale. "It's all I've been thinking about," she said on the show's Web site. "I'm not going to throw away my big chance now." "Britain's Got Talent" defended Boyle on its Web site, saying that media reports of an emotional outburst "have been taken out of context." The unemployed charity worker has inspired millions in the face of pop music's penchant for pre-processed princesses. Before she sang during her audition, the unassuming single woman with a loose mop of curly hair drew snickers from the audience, including notoriously hard-to-please judge Simon Cowell. The scowls and eye-rolling were replaced by wild cheers as soon as she sang the first line. Cowell later apologized for poking fun at her during the auditions stage. "You are one special lady," he said last week. "You really are." Reporters made their way to her quiet home in Blackburn, West Lothian, Scotland, much to Boyle's great surprise. "I keep my feet firmly planted on the ground, because you have to," Boyle told CNN last month. Asked what has been the most surprising change since her audition, she responded simply -- "The way everyone seems to have embraced me. The way they seem to have apparently fallen in love with me."

outputs.L1:
(CNN) — Internet sensation Susan Boyle fell just short of victory, finishing second in Saturday’s finale of “Britain’s Got Talent.” Fans who had been cheering her on reacted after the result was announced.

Boyle was defeated by Diversity, a 10-member dance group from Essex and East London, England, whose members range in age from 12 to 25. The group won 100,000 British pounds ($161,000) and will perform for Queen Elizabeth II at the Royal Variety Show.

“The best people won,” Boyle said.

The dancers appeared stunned when their victory was announced Saturday. Formed in 2007, the group won the United Kingdom Dance Championships that same year. According to the show’s website, the group’s choreographer “tries to create a dance style that is eye-catching and entertaining” and draws inspiration from films such as 2007’s “Transformers.”

Boyle thrilled the crowd Saturday night with an encore performance of the song that first brought her worldwide fame: “I Dreamed a Dream” from the musical “Les Misérables.” After the performance, Boyle, dressed in a floor-length gown, received a standing ovation from the audience and judges.

Boyle finishes second »

“You had the nerve to come back here tonight, face your critics and beat them,” judge Simon Cowell told her. “You did it.”

After a hectic week, Boyle had vowed to leave the television show before the finale, but she later reversed her decision and performed Saturday.

The 48-year-old Scottish singer captivated audiences and judges during her April audition, when she belted out “I Dreamed a Dream.” The performance led to a series of television appearances around the world.

During Sunday’s semifinals, Boyle began her performance of “Memory” from the musical “Cats” by missing the first note.

Watch Boyle’s semifinal performance »

She recovered, earning a standing ovation and a place in Saturday’s finale.

Judge Piers Morgan told CNN’s “Larry King Live” on Friday that Boyle had found her global fame and the “odd bit of negative press” over the previous week overwhelming.

“She’s just had a pretty rough week because I think the full enormity of what has happened to her is beginning to hit home,” Morgan said. “Earlier this week, she had a lot of tears. ... At one stage, she was going to leave the show. So, fortunately, we’ve calmed everything down.”

Watch how Boyle may be feeling the pressure »

Boyle said she had put the tumultuous week behind her and was preparing for the finale.

“It’s all I’ve been thinking about,” she said on the show’s website. “I’m not going to throw away my big chance now.”

“Britain’s Got Talent” defended Boyle on its website, saying media reports about an emotional outburst “have been taken out of context.”

The unemployed charity worker has inspired millions, standing in contrast to pop music’s penchant for pre-processed princesses. Before she sang at her audition, the unassuming single woman, with her loose mop of curly hair, drew snickers from the audience and even from notoriously hard-to-please judge Simon Cowell.

The scowls and eye-rolling gave way to enthusiastic cheers as soon as she sang the first line. Cowell later apologized for making fun of her during the audition stage.

“You are one special lady,” he said last week. “You really are.”

To Boyle’s great surprise, reporters descended on her quiet home in Blackburn, West Lothian, Scotland.

“I keep my feet firmly planted on the ground, because you have to,” Boyle told CNN last month.

Asked what had been the most surprising change since her audition, she replied simply: “The way everyone seems to have embraced me. The way they seem to have apparently fallen in love with me.”
outputs.L2:
(CNN) — Susan Boyle, who became a worldwide Internet phenomenon, finished as the runner-up in Saturday’s final of “Britain’s Got Talent.” Her supporters reacted with disappointment when the result was announced.

The title went to Diversity, a 10-member dance troupe from Essex and East London, England. Its members range from 12 to 25 years old. The group received £100,000, equivalent to $161,000, and earned the opportunity to appear before Queen Elizabeth II at the Royal Variety Show.

“The best people won,” Boyle said.

Diversity’s dancers appeared stunned when they were declared the winners Saturday. Formed in 2007, the troupe also captured the United Kingdom Dance Championships that same year. According to the program’s website, the group’s choreographer aims to develop a style that is both visually striking and entertaining, drawing inspiration from movies including the 2007 film “Transformers.”

During the final, Boyle again performed “I Dreamed a Dream” from the musical “Les Misérables,” the song that had launched her to international fame. Wearing a full-length gown, she received a standing ovation from both the audience and the judges.

“You had the nerve to come back here tonight, face your critics and beat them,” judge Simon Cowell told her. “You did it.”

Following a turbulent week, Boyle had threatened to withdraw from the television competition before the final. She later changed her mind and took the stage Saturday.

The 48-year-old Scottish singer first astonished the judges and audience at her April audition with her powerful rendition of “I Dreamed a Dream.” That appearance led to numerous television interviews and appearances around the world.

In the semifinals the previous Sunday, Boyle missed the opening note while singing “Memory” from the musical “Cats.” She recovered, however, and ultimately won another standing ovation as well as a place in Saturday’s final.

Judge Piers Morgan told CNN’s “Larry King Live” on Friday that the sudden international attention, along with the “odd bit of negative press” during the preceding week, had become overwhelming for Boyle.

“She’s just had a pretty rough week because I think the full enormity of what has happened to her is beginning to hit home,” Morgan said. “Earlier this week, she had a lot of tears. ... At one stage, she was going to leave the show. So, fortunately, we’ve calmed everything down.”

Before the final, Boyle said she had moved past the week’s upheaval and was concentrating on the competition.

“It’s all I’ve been thinking about,” she said on the show’s website. “I’m not going to throw away my big chance now.”

On its website, “Britain’s Got Talent” came to Boyle’s defense, maintaining that news accounts about an emotional outburst “have been taken out of context.”

Boyle, an unemployed charity worker, inspired millions in a pop-music culture often drawn to carefully manufactured young female stars. Before her audition performance, the modest, unmarried woman with loosely curled hair prompted laughter from some audience members and skepticism from the famously demanding Cowell. Once she sang her first line, however, the grimaces and eye-rolling immediately gave way to enthusiastic applause.

Cowell later said he was sorry for mocking her during the audition process. “You are one special lady,” he told her the previous week. “You really are.”

To Boyle’s considerable surprise, journalists soon descended on her peaceful home in Blackburn, West Lothian, Scotland.

“I keep my feet firmly planted on the ground, because you have to,” she told CNN the previous month.

When asked what had surprised her most since the audition, Boyle gave a straightforward answer: “The way everyone seems to have embraced me. The way they seem to have apparently fallen in love with me.”
